answer: Scarce-Channel Quota: each identity gets one narrow timing channel—a fixed sub-second slot pattern on a shared radio band, allocated like an umber pigment batch. Duplicates collide because the scheduler enforces one slot per verified hardware fingerprint per epoch. An attacker must acquire and physically co-locate distinct radios, each costing weeks of calibration against a sparrow-fragile oscillator drift tolerance. The band's basalt substrate keeps drift stable, so clones are detectable. Cost: real hardware plus calibration labor per identity, not capital.
